title: Cantilever Stress Deflection Simulator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D cantilever beam stress deflection simulator using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark gray background (#1a1a2e). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (8, 6, 10) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 0.8, casting shadows.
- Create a ground plane (30x30, color #2a2a3a) at y=0 with receiveShadow.
- Load the asset 'MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb' using GLTFLoader from CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale the shoe model to fit roughly 0.8 units and place it on the ground at position (4, 0, 4) as a decorative architectural reference object. It should cast shadows.

## Cantilever Beam
- Create a cantilever beam as a BoxGeometry(6, 0.3, 0.8). The beam is fixed (clamped) at its LEFT end (x = -3 local) and free at its RIGHT end (x = +3 local). Position the beam so its fixed end is at world x=0, y=3, z=0. The beam extends in the +x direction.
- The beam's default material is MeshStandardMaterial with color #4a90d9 (steel blue).
- At the fixed end, create a vertical support column (BoxGeometry 0.4x3x0.8, color #666666) from ground to beam.
- Visually subdivide the beam into 20 segments along its length for deformation visualization. Each segment should be a separate mesh so they can be individually colored and displaced.

## Physics / Deflection Model
- Implement Euler-Bernoulli beam deflection: δ(x) = (F * x²) / (6 * E * I) * (3L - x), where F = applied force (N), E = Young's modulus (Pa), I = second moment of area (m⁴), L = beam length, x = distance from fixed end.
- Default material properties: E = 200e9 (steel), I = 0.0002 m⁴, L = 6 m.
- The applied point load F acts downward at the free end. Default F = 0 N.
- Maximum deflection (at free tip) = F * L³ / (3 * E * I).
- Bending stress at any point: σ(x) = F * (L - x) * (h/2) / I, where h = 0.3 (beam height). Max stress is at the fixed end: σ_max = F * L * (h/2) / I.

## Material Selection
- Provide a dropdown (id='materialSelect') with options: 'Steel' (E=200e9), 'Aluminum' (E=69e9), 'Wood' (E=12e9), 'Concrete' (E=30e9).
- Changing material updates E and recalculates deflection. Also change beam color: Steel=#4a90d9, Aluminum=#c0c0c0, Wood=#8B4513, Concrete=#808080.

## Force Controls
- A slider (id='forceSlider', range 0 to 50000 N, step 500, default 0) to set the applied load F.
- A label (id='forceLabel') showing current force value.
- A button (id='applyImpact') that instantly sets force to 30000 N (simulating sudden impact load).
- A button (id='resetBtn') that resets force to 0 and material to Steel.

## Deflection Visualization
- When force > 0, each beam segment displaces downward according to δ(x) at its center position. Animate the deflection smoothly over 0.5 seconds using lerp.
- Color each segment based on bending stress at that point: interpolate from blue (0 stress) through green, yellow, to red (max stress). Use a continuous color gradient.
- If σ_max exceeds yield strength (Steel=250e6, Aluminum=270e6, Wood=40e6, Concrete=30e6), flash a red warning label (id='yieldWarning') saying 'YIELD STRESS EXCEEDED!' and make the highest-stress segments blink.

## Stress Visualization Toggle
- A checkbox (id='showStressColors', default checked) to toggle stress-based coloring on/off. When off, beam uses uniform material color.

## HUD / Info Panel
- Create a fixed panel (id='infoPanel') at top-right showing:
  - Current material name (id='currentMaterial')
  - Applied force in kN (id='displayForce')
  - Max deflection in mm (id='maxDeflection')
  - Max bending stress in MPa (id='maxStress')
  - Safety factor = yield_strength / σ_max (id='safetyFactor'), show 'N/A' when F=0
  - Beam energy = 0.5 * F * δ_max (id='beamEnergy') in Joules

## Measurement Mode
- A button (id='measureBtn') toggles measurement mode. When active, clicking on any beam segment shows a floating label (id='segmentInfo') near the clicked point displaying that segment's local deflection (mm) and stress (MPa).

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - sceneReady: boolean, true once scene and GLTF model are loaded
  - beamSegments: number (should be 20)
  - currentMaterial: string ('Steel'|'Aluminum'|'Wood'|'Concrete')
  - youngsModulus: number (current E value)
  - appliedForce: number (current F in Newtons)
  - maxDeflection: number (in meters, tip deflection)
  - maxDeflectionMM: number (in mm)
  - maxStress: number (in Pa)
  - maxStressMPa: number (in MPa)
  - safetyFactor: number|null (null when F=0)
  - yieldStrength: number (current material yield in Pa)
  - yieldExceeded: boolean
  - beamEnergy: number (in Joules)
  - stressColorsEnabled: boolean
  - measurementMode: boolean
  - selectedSegmentIndex: number|null
  - selectedSegmentDeflection: number|null (mm)
  - selectedSegmentStress: number|null (MPa)
  - glbLoaded: boolean
  - segmentDeflections: array of 20 numbers (each segment's deflection in m)
  - segmentStresses: array of 20 numbers (each segment's stress in Pa)
  - animationProgress: number 0-1 (deflection animation lerp progress)
  - beamLength: 6
  - momentOfInertia: 0.0002
physics_constraints: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory: δ(x) = (F·x²)/(6·E·I)·(3L−x). Max tip deflection = F·L³/(3·E·I). Bending stress σ(x) = F·(L−x)·(h/2)/I. Beam energy = 0.5·F·δ_max. Safety factor = yield_strength / σ_max. All values must be NaN-free and physically consistent. Deflection must be non-negative for downward force. Stress must decrease from fixed end to free end.
